description:
fz-wof routed the two doors it named -- native_codegen/receive.rs emit_region_test and ir_interp/backend.rs AssertTuple -- through RuntimeTypePredicate::tuple_arity(n) and the shared matcher/emitter, and deleted their hand-written schema compares. src/ir_interp/dispatch_exec.rs ~348 still answers Region::TupleArity with its own chain: kind() == ValueKind::STRUCT plus struct_schema_id(p) == interp_tuple_schema_id(runtime, arity), after the lane-form fast path.

It was left out of fz-wof because of the type parameter, not because this door avoids the predicate layer -- its Region::Type arm does reach whole_value_matches_predicate, through the injected type_match closure. execute_dispatch_node and dispatch_region_hit are generic over TypeHandle (dispatch_exec.rs ~88, ~312) and the closure's signature is FnMut(&mut IrInterpRuntime, &Module, &TypeHandle, &BackendBoundValue) -> Result<bool, DispatchStop>, so the arity arm has a Ty in hand and no way to reach a RuntimeTypePredicate::tuple_arity(n) through it. Projecting one here would need &mut Types at a call site that does not carry it, and synthesising a Ty for 'a tuple of arity n' re-poses the question in the wrong layer.

The fold wants the region evaluator to ask RuntimeTypePredicate questions directly rather than through a Ty-shaped hole -- which is also what would let the two interpreter doors share one region evaluator. Check against fz-gee.7 before starting: that ticket deletes the NATIVE receive executor by lowering the matcher through fz_ir dispatch, and may leave this interpreter one answering fz_ir-lowered questions instead, in which case this reading disappears with it rather than needing its own fold.
title: Region::TupleArity has a fourth reading in the interpreter's receive dispatch executor
